cards.explanation: The answer is Judah. God tells Ezekiel to write, "Belonging to Judah and to the Israelites associated with him." (Ezekiel 37:16). So the first stick has Judah's name on it, plus the Israelites with him. Ezekiel is basically running a tiny label shop.

The answer is True. God says, "Then join them together into one stick, so that they become one in your hand." (Ezekiel 37:17). Ezekiel takes two sticks and then gets told to join them into one. I'd have been standing there asking where the tape was.

The answer is False. When the people ask, Ezekiel is told to tell them "…this is what the Lord GOD says…" (Ezekiel 37:19). The explanation comes from God, not from Ezekiel's own thinking. Honestly, that's a relief for anybody who has ever been put on the spot with a question.

The answer is hand. God says, "I will make them into a single stick, and they will become one in My hand." (Ezekiel 37:19). Earlier the sticks were one in Ezekiel's hand, and here God says they become one in His. That's the whole point of the sticks, friends.

The answer is into their own land. God says, "I will take the Israelites out of the nations to which they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them into their own land." (Ezekiel 37:21). He gathers them from every direction and brings them home. I think I'd have kissed the ground.
The answer is king. God says, "…one king will rule over all of them." (Ezekiel 37:22). One nation, one king. Two kingdoms used to mean two sets of everything, and that's a lot of paperwork.

The answer is False. God says they "…will no longer be two nations and will never again be divided into two kingdoms." (Ezekiel 37:22). Never means never, friends. Once God makes them one nation, they stay one.

The answer is that they will be His people and He will be their God. After saying He will cleanse them, God says, "Then they will be My people, and I will be their God." (Ezekiel 37:23). It's the closest, warmest line in the whole passage. I'd put it on the front of a cookie box.

The answer is David. God says, "My servant David will be king over them, and there will be one shepherd for all of them." (Ezekiel 37:24). David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), and here God calls him His servant. That's a title worth having, friends.

The answer is peace. God says, "…I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant." (Ezekiel 37:26). A covenant of peace that lasts forever. I could use some of that in my kitchen on batch day.
The answer is the nations. God says, "Then the nations will know that I the LORD sanctify Israel…" (Ezekiel 37:28). The nations are the ones who will know. That's a lot of nations learning one thing.
